fatal_errors: The proposed perturbation method is not explicitly free energy perturbation between MTP and DFT; it instead allows thermodynamic integration over a reduced coupling parameter or from a harmonic reference.
The material is changed from nominal TaVCrW to an unspecified Ta-based quinary alloy, so composition-specific electronic, short-range-order, and functional effects are lost.
The claimed greater-than-90% saving and less-than-5% error are unsupported and do not reproduce the relevant 80% saving, approximately 20-fold speedup, and sub-0.5 meV/atom free-energy criterion.

The assertion that full thermodynamic integration has exponential scaling is scientifically misleading; the central difficulty is sampling cost and slow convergence rather than a generic exponential scaling law.
explanation: The hypothesis correctly identifies the main problem and broadly reconstructs the replacement of an EAM-based reference by a Moment Tensor Potential to make perturbative free-energy calculations practical. It also recognizes the principal potential failure mode: inadequate coverage of high-temperature liquid and composition-dependent environments can cause extrapolation and deceptively cheap but biased sampling. However, it never clearly states the target MTP-to-DFT FEP estimator or the key requirement of small energy-difference variance and phase-space overlap. It omits the specified TaVCrW composition, 0 GPa condition, 2000–2400 K range, 12×12×12 cell, GGA-PBE/LDA comparison, sub-1 meV/atom training accuracy, electronic Gibbs contribution, DOS feature, and 2.4 meV/atom SRO stabilization. Its outcome metrics are substantially looser or numerically inconsistent with the target. The falsification design is useful: comparison against reduced-cell DFT-TI, liquid structural observables, timing, and a liquid-excluded training-set ablation can distinguish genuine acceleration from training-set leakage or extrapolation. It would be stronger if it benchmarked FEP against TI on the same configurations and composition, measured the distribution and variance of DFT-minus-MTP energies, required agreement within 0.5 meV/atom, and reported effective sample size. The cited evidence supports only the general cost–accuracy merits of MTPs in MoNbTaW and dislocation applications; it does not validate liquid free energies, FEP, TaVCrW melting, or the numerical performance claims.
